newsitem.title: USA: US to stay out of heat oil market for now -O'Leary. [corrected 08:13 gmt 19/10]
newsitem.headline: US to stay out of heat oil market for now -O'Leary. [corrected 08:13 gmt 19/10]

text.p: The U.S. government has no plans for now to buy heating oil to help build up supplies in case of a shortage this winter, Energy Secretary Hazel O'Leary said Friday.

"On the question of distillate we've reached the conclusion for the near term that the market certainly does not need Big Brother as a big buyer," she said, following a meeting with 14 oil and gas industry executives.
O'Leary called the meeting last week to discuss the supply and demand outlook for heating fuels this winter amid concern over historically low heating oil stocks.
O'Leary said that at least two companies had agreed to take steps to help boost output of heating oil, which refiners are currently producing at around 3.6 million barrels per day.
Citgo executives said they would postpone planned maintenance on a catalytic cracker, she said. (Corrects from "Texaco Inc executives" to "Citgo exceutives")
Tosco said it planned to maximize its refinery output earlier than normal, she added.

Responding to a proposal by Rep. Joe Kennedy, D-Massachusetts, O'Leary said she had called for the Energy Department to study the feasibility of setting up regional product reserves to cope with emergencies.
